Subject "League of Chinese and Japanese Youths, China Headquarters"
(中日青年聯盟中國總部) - inaugurated
Made by D. I. Pan Lien Pih Forwarded by C. Crawford

Under the auspices of Mr. Zung Siu-foo (陳修夫),
Commissioner of the Bureau of Education of the Shanghai
City Government, in conjunction with some Japanese subjects,
the "League of Chinese and Japanese Youths, China Head-
quarters" was inaugurated at a meeting held between 1 p.m.
and 4 p.m. on February, 12, 1939 in the Japanese Primary
School, North Szechuen Road, which was attended by some
300 Japanese elementary school children and some 700
Chinese primary school students from schools in Nantao,
Pootung and Chapei. At the conclusion of this inaugural
meeting, the following slogans ( a copy of the printed
slogans attached ) were shouted :-
1) Spiritual unity for Chinese and Japanese youths!
2) Establish peace in the East Asia!
3) Unity for Chinese and Japanese youths!
4) Chinese and Japanese youths should endeavour to
cooperate!
5) Solve the distressing problem of unemployment!
6) Rescue the unemployed population of East Asia!
7) Exert our combined efforts at mutual existence and
mutual prosperity!

Pan Lien - pih
D. I.

February 13, 1939. Afternoon Translation.

Sin Shun Pao (Japanese owned Chinese language newspaper)
dated Feb. 12:

SHANGHAI NEW CHINA YOUTHS' ASSOCIATION

At about 10 a.m. February 11, the Shanghai
Headquarters of the Sino-Japanese Youths' League held its
inaugural meeting in its auditorium in Yung Feng Fong
(永丰坊), North Szechuen Road. Amongst those present
were Tokomoto of the Japanese Special Service Department,
Nagashima, advisor to the Bureau of Social Affairs, and
students of the Pootung Primary School.
After a report was made by Wong Yu-shi
(王雨軒), who presided, speeches were delivered by
Chinese and Japanese officials.
At the close, the following slogans were
shouted:-
1) "Chinese and Japanese youths, unite."
2) "Establish peace in East Asia."
3) "Chinese and Japanese youths, co-operate strenuously."
4) "Remove all the hardships of the unemployed."
5) "Relieve the unemployed in East Asia."
The League was formed through co-operation
between Chinese and Japanese youths.
The League has now been renamed the Shanghai
New China Youths' Association (上海新中國青年會).

Subject Japanese Military Students Proceeding Through Settlement on

Made by F.S.190 S.H.Holtam Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
On Sunday, 4th December 1938, the undersigned, accompanied by
J.P.S.73, S. Katayama were ordered by Inspr. Leslie to be at the
Great Western Road Railway Crossing by 4.30p.m. to escort some
trucks containing Japanese Military Students who wished to
proceed along Settlement Roads to the Garden Bridge. The
Students about 90 in number arrived at the crossing at about
5 p.m. in three Motor Trucks, but remained on the Western side of
the crossing while they attempted to repair one of the trucks
which was out of order.

While waiting J.P.S.73 accompanied by a Japanese Officer
approached me and asked if the trucks could proceed by way of
B'well and Nanking Roads. I replied that they could, but
suggested that it would be quicker if they went by way of Avenue
Joffre, Wei-hai-wei and Foochow Roads. A conversation then took
place between J.P.S.73 and the Officer, following which the
J.P.S. informed me that the officer wished to proceed by way of
B'well and Nanking Roads, and I agreed to lead them by this route.

At about 5.40p.m. having failed to repair the disabled truck
the students crowded into the remaining two trucks and J.P.S.73
informed me that they were ready to proceed. I then escorted them
by way of Gt.Western Road, B'Well Road, Nanking Road and The Bund
to the Garden Bridge, arriving there at about 6.05p.m.

The procession travelled in the following order, re myself
and J.P.S.73 in the lead on a Motor Cycle followed by a Baby Aus-
tin Motor Car bearing S.D.F. plates and containing 3 officers with
the two trucks bringing up the rear. I did not observe any
untoward incidents while I was escorting them.

Your obedient servant,
[Signature]
A.C.(Traffic). F.S.190.

由 F.S.190 S.H.Holtam 制作 经 [签名] 转呈

先生，
1938年12月4日星期日，在下与 J.P.S.73，片山 (S. Katayama) 奉莱斯利 (Leslie) 巡官之命，于下午4时30分前到达大西路铁路道口，护送载有希望沿租界道路前往外白渡桥的日本军校学生的几辆卡车。约90名学生于下午5时许乘坐三辆摩托卡车到达道口，但因其中一辆卡车发生故障，他们试图修理，故停留在道口西侧。

等待期间，J.P.S.73 陪同一名日本军官走近我，询问卡车是否可以通过勃威尔路 (B'well Road) 和南京路行驶。我回答说可以，但建议如果他们走霞飞路 (Avenue Joffre)、威海卫路和福州路会更快。随后 J.P.S.73 与该军官进行了交谈，之后 J.P.S. 告知我，该军官希望经由勃威尔路和南京路行驶，我同意按此路线引导他们。

下午5时40分左右，因未能修好故障卡车，学生们挤进剩下的两辆卡车，J.P.S.73 通知我他们已准备出发。随后我经由大西路、勃威尔路、南京路和外滩护送他们前往外白渡桥，于下午6时05分左右到达。

队伍行进顺序如下，我和 J.P.S.73 骑摩托车在前导引，随后是一辆挂有 S.D.F. 牌照的 Baby Austin 小汽车，车内载有3名军官，两辆卡车殿后。在护送期间，我没有观察到任何意外事件。

您忠实的仆人，
[签名]
交通科助理总监。 F.S.190。

Pro-Japanese Propaganda
- - - - - - - - - - -

During the evening of December 4, between 5.40 p.m.
and 7 p.m., copies of four different kinds of handbills
were distributed by Japanese soldiers from two military
trucks (No. unknown), while proceeding East on Nanking Road
and Bubbling Well Road near the following places :-
(1) Bubbling Well Road near Carter Road and
Love Lane (5.40 p.m.)
(2) Nanking Road, near Yu Ya Ching Road (5.47 p.m.)
(3) Nanking Road near Kiangse Road (7 p.m.)
Two of these handbills purport to emanate from the "Asia
Youth League ( 亞細亞青年同盟 )," one from the
Ishin Institution, now situated at the former site of
Futan University, Kiangwan, and one which does not give
the source of origin.
Apart from the pro-Japanese propaganda contained
therein, one which is entitled "An Advice to the Shanghai
Brethren" urges the Chinese to abrogate the extraterritoriality
rights now enjoyed by the foreigners, and to take back the
Settlements.
Attached to this report are four copies of the handbills
together with translation.

Certified true copy

H. C. Lardley

(3) 南京路靠近江西路 (Kiangse Road) 处（下午7时）
其中两份传单声称出自“亚细亚青年同盟 ( 亞細亞青年同盟 )”，一份出自位于江湾原复旦大学址的维新学院 (Ishin Institution)，还有一份未注明出处。
除其中包含的亲日宣传内容外，一份题为《告上海同胞书》的传单敦促中国人废除外国人目前享有的治外法权，并收回租界。
本报告附有这四份传单的副本及其译文。

page_data.en:
Translation of a handbill entitled "Back to the Native Place".
----------------------------------------------
The problem of how to get back to your native places
must have already entered your thoughts. Your failure to solve
this problem would appear to be the result of false propaganda
issued by the newspapers. You should know already that the news
being circulated by the newspapers printed in the Settlement is
not reliable. They are mouthpieces of the Kuomintang Government,
and their object is to induce you to become their tools. All
the news contained therein is fabricated. The facts which were
placed before you with regard to the fall of Nanking, Hsuchow,
Hankow and Canton serve as a good illustration and prove that
those newspapers supplied the public with false stories in which
they related victories for the Chinese Forces. Any one with
common sense must realize now the tricks these newspapers have
played.

The situation at present is normal in the inland
cities and the propaganda circulated by the newspapers in connec-
tion with the activities of guerillas and the atrocities of the
Japanese soldiers are all contrary to facts. Not only the
inland cities enjoy peace, but there is also a sufficient supply
of provisions, clothes and other daily necessities, and at cheap-
er prices than those prevailing in Shanghai.

The people living in Shanghai should not be hoodwinked
further by the propaganda fabricated by the Kuomintang newspapers.
We personally know of the peaceful state in the inland cities as
we have just come from those places. District governments have
been established, communication has been restored, and schools
have been re-opened - furthermore, farmers' cooperative societies
are in the course of formation and arrangements are being made
to grant loans to the merchants in order to enable them to carry
on their business.

Be prepared immediately to return to your lovely and
long-departed native places.
Certified true copy.
H. C. Eardley
Asia Youth League,
December 3.
page_data.zh:
题为《回到故乡》的传单译文。
----------------------------------------------
如何回到你们故乡的问题一定已经进入了你们的思绪。你们未能解决这个问题，似乎是报纸发布的虚假宣传所致。你们应该已经知道，租界内印刷的报纸所传播的消息是不可靠的。它们是国民党政府的喉舌，其目的是诱使你们成为他们的工具。其中包含的所有新闻都是捏造的。关于南京、徐州、汉口和广州陷落的情况向你们展示的事实就是很好的例证，证明这些报纸向公众提供了编造中国军队获胜的虚假故事。任何有常识的人现在都必须意识到这些报纸所耍弄的花招。

目前内地城市局势正常，报纸上散布的关于游击队活动和日本士兵暴行的宣传都与事实相悖。不仅内地城市享有和平，而且粮食、衣物和其他日常必需品供应充足，价格也比上海 prevailing 的价格便宜。

居住在上海的人们不应再被国民党报纸捏造的宣传所蒙蔽。我们个人了解内地城市的和平状态，因为我们刚从那些地方回来。区政府已经建立，通讯已经恢复，学校已经重新开学——此外，农民合作社正在组建中，并正在安排向商人提供贷款，以便使他们能够继续经营业务。

立即准备好返回你们可爱且久别的故乡。
认证无误副本。
H. C. Eardley
亚细亚青年联盟，
12月3日。

Translation of a handbill entitled "Do Not Fear the
Japanese - but cooperate with them in the manner
of righteousness".
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

Dear fellow countrymen,

Despite the removal of the scene
of hostilities, the people of New China appear to be
still reluctant in trusting the Japanese soldiers and
Japanese merchants. Because of fear, they maintain an
obedient attitude, even although in certain cases the
Japanese are wrong. Such an attitude is deemed incorrect,
and we should maintain our self-dignity and work hand in
hand with the Japanese in the spirit of righteousness.
The Japanese are our brothers, the only difference between
us being that they are educated and have excellent
organizing ability. We should repent and change our
attitude towards them which we previously held. From
this date, we should cooperate in the manner of a big
family - (East Asia) - with our sister nation.
Dear fellow countrymen, there is only one way which
stands before us and that is to be friendly towards
the Japanese and to keep in close touch with them.

Ishin Institute.
December 3.

Certified true copy

H. C. Lardley

WPY/.

题为“不要害怕日本人——要以正义的方式与他们合作”的传单译文。
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

亲爱的同胞们，

尽管战事已经远离，新中国的人民似乎仍然不愿信任日本士兵和日本商人。出于恐惧，他们保持着顺从的态度，即使在某些情况下是日本人错了。这种态度被认为是错误的，我们应该保持自尊，本着正义的精神与日本人携手合作。日本人是我们的兄弟，我们之间唯一的区别在于他们受过教育并拥有出色的组织能力。我们应该悔悟并改变此前对他们持有的态度。从今天起，我们应该以大家庭（东亚）的方式与我们的姐妹之邦合作。
亲爱的同胞们，摆在我们面前的只有一条路，那就是对日本人友好并与他们保持密切联系。

维新学院。
12月3日。

经核证无误副本

H. C. Lardley

WPY/.

page_data.en:
Translation of a handbill entitled "An advice to Shanghai
Brethren"
----------------------------------------------

Dear Brethren,

        It is within our expectations that when this
handbills reaches you, you will immediately throw it away
without a perusal, and will further abuse the distributors
as "traitors" and "swine." But we implore you to keep
your temper, and spend a few minutes in reading the
handbill, because it dwells upon the problems which
immediately affect your.

        Dear brethren, we are also the enthusiastic
youth of China with hot blood in our veins, but our present
concern is for the welfare of the Chinese Race. We are by
no means selfish. We fully realize who our enemies are.
Do you realise that you are living under the protection
of "White People"? Then you must know who our enemies are.
Who are the people responsible for the present war. Who
are the people standing by our side with base ideas and
watching for a chance to obtain privileges out of the war?
It is true that Japan is fighting for her existence, but
on the other hand, she is fighting because she cannot
tolerate seeing the Chinese people who are of the same
race being exploited and oppressed by an alien people.
You are still living under the genuine enemy and at their
mercy - but do you think that such condition can last long
which permits a feeling of patriotism in carrying out
national salvation work? The truth is that the Settlements
are the places, where national sovereignty has been lost.
It is a national humiliation. Let us eradicate this and
advocate (1) the Great Asia Munro Doctrine (2) the abrogation
of extraterritoriality, and (3) rendition of Settlements.

                                Asia Youth League.

                                December 3.

Certified true copy
H.C. Fardley
page_data.zh:
题为“致上海兄弟书”的传单译文
----------------------------------------------

亲爱的兄弟们，

        我们可以预料，当这份传单送到你们手中时，你们会看也不看就立刻把它扔掉，并进一步辱骂分发者为“汉奸”和“猪猡”。但我们恳请你们克制脾气，花几分钟阅读这份传单，因为它论述的是直接影响你们的问题。

        亲爱的兄弟们，我们也是热血沸腾的中国热情青年，但我们目前关心的是中华民族的福祉。我们绝非自私。我们充分清楚谁是我们的敌人。你们是否意识到你们生活在“白人”的保护之下？那么你们必须知道谁是我们的敌人。谁是造成当前战争的人？谁是怀着卑鄙念头站在我们身旁、伺机从战争中获取特权的人？诚然，日本是为了其生存而战，但另一方面，她之所以作战，是因为她不能容忍看到同种族的中国人民被异族剥削和压迫。你们仍然生活在真正的敌人之下，任其摆布——但你们认为这种允许在进行救国工作时怀有爱国情感的状况能持续很久吗？事实是，租界是丧失国家主权的地方。这是国耻。让我们消除这一耻辱，并倡导（1）大亚洲门罗主义（2）废除治外法权，以及（3）归还租界。

                                亚洲青年同盟。

                                12月3日。

经核证无误副本
H.C. Fardley

Subject Pro-Japanese Propaganda

Made by C.D.I. Sih Tse-liang Forwarded by C. Crawford. A. I.

During the evening of December 4, between 5.40 p.m.
and 7 p.m., copies of four different kinds of handbills
were distributed by Japanese soldiers from two military
trucks (No. unknown), while proceeding East on Nanking Road
and Bubbling Well Road near the following places :-
(1) Bubbling Well Road near Carter Road and
Love Lane (5.40 p.m.)
(2) Nanking Road, near Yu Ya Ching Road (5.47 p.m.)
(3) Nanking Road near Kiangse Road (7 p.m.).

Two of these handbills purport to emanate from the "Asia
Youth League (亞細亞青年同盟 )," one from the
Ishin Institution, now situated at the former site of
Futan University, Kiangwan, and one which does not give
the source of origin.

Apart from the pro-Japanese propaganda contained
therein, one which is entitled "An Advice to the Shanghai
Brethren" urges the Chinese to abrogate the extraterritoriality
rights now enjoyed by the foreigners, and to take back the
Settlements.

Attached to this report are four copies of the
handbills together with translation.

The problem of how to get back to your native
places must have already entered your thoughts. Your
failure to solve this problem would appear to be the
result of false propaganda issued by the newspapers.
You should know already that the news being circulated
by the newspapers printed in the Settlement is not
reliable. They are mouthpieces of the Kuomintang
Government, and their object is to induce you to become
their tools. All the news contained therein is fabricated.
The facts which were placed before you with regard to the
fall of Nanking, Hsuchow, Hankow and Canton serve as a
good illustration and prove that those newspapers supplied
the public with false stories in which they related
victories for the Chinese Forces. Any one with common
sense must realize now the tricks these newspapers have
played.

The situation at present is normal in the inland
cities and the propaganda circulated by the newspapers in

atrocities of the Japanese soldiers are all contrary to
facts. Not only the inland cities enjoy peace, but there

prevailing in Shanghai.

re-opened - furthermore, farmers' cooperative societies

Dear Brethren,
It is within our expectations that when this
handbills reaches you, you will immediately throw it away
without a perusal, and will further abuse the distributors
as "traitors" and "swine." But we implore you to keep
your temper, and spend a few minutes in reading the
handbill, because it dwells upon the problems which
immediately affect your.
Dear brethren, we are also the enthusiastic
youth of China with hot blood in our veins, but our present
concern is for the welfare of the Chinese Race. We are by
no means selfish. We fully realize who our enemies are.
Do you realise that you are living under the protection
of "White People"? Then you must know who our enemies are.
Who are the people responsible for the present war. Who
are the people standing by our side with base ideas and
watching for a chance to obtain privileges out of the war?
It is true that Japan is fighting for her existence, but
on the other hand, she is fighting because she cannot
tolerate seeing the Chinese people who are of the same
race being exploited and oppressed by an alien people.
You are still living under the genuine enemy and at their
mercy - but do you think that such condition can last long
which permits a feeling of patriotism in carrying out
national salvation work? The truth is that the Settlements
are the places, where national sovereignty has been lost.

advocate (1) the Great Asia Munro Doctrine (2) the abrogation
of extraterritoriality, and (3) rendition of Settlements.

Asia Youth League.

The problem of how to get back to your native places
must have already entered your thoughts. Your failure to solve
this problem would appear to be the result of false propaganda
issued by the newspapers. You should know already that the news
being circulated by the newspapers printed in the Settlement is
not reliable. They are mouthpieces of the Kuomintang Government,
and their object is to induce you to become their tools. All
the news contained therein is fabricated. The facts which were
placed before you with regard to the fall of Nanking, Hsuchow,
Hankow and Canton serve as a good illustration and prove that
those newspapers supplied the public with false stories in which
they related victories for the Chinese Forces. Any one with
common sense must realize now the tricks these newspapers have
played.

The situation at present is normal in the inland
cities and the propaganda circulated by the newspapers in connec-
tion with the activities of guerillas and the atrocities of the
Japanese soldiers are all contrary to facts. Not only the
inland cities enjoy peace, but there is also a sufficient supply
of provisions, clothes and other daily necessities, and at cheap-
er prices than those prevailing in Shanghai.

The people living in Shanghai should not be hoodwinked
further by the propaganda fabricated by the Kuomintang newspapers.
We personally know of the peaceful state in the inland cities as
we have just come from those places. District governments have
been established, communication has been restored, and schools
have been re-opened - furthermore, farmers' cooperative societies
are in the course of formation and arrangements are being made
to grant loans to the merchants in order to enable them to carry
on their business.

Be prepared immediately to return to your lovely and
long-departed native places.

Certified true copy.                      Asia Youth League,
                                          December 5.
H. C. Eardley
